raw_graphql_pull_request.body: ## Motivation Enable Qwen3.8-Flash-Next inference on NPU with Qwen Sparse Attention (QSA), graph replay, and NEXTN/MTP speculative decoding, building on the mainline model support from [#37500](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/37500). Dependency: [sgl-project/sgl-kernel-npu#807](https://github.com/sgl-project/sgl-kernel-npu/pull/807) provides the production kernels. Before merging, an installable kernel package containing these modules and the corresponding SGLang dependency must be verified together; local source-tree validation does not establish release-package availability. ## Modifications - Reuse shared QSA indexer orchestration on NPU, preserving per-query bounds, padding, MTP index reuse, and logical-to-physical KV mapping. - Integrate six operator groups from `sgl_kernel_npu.qwen3_8_flash_next`: PLE short convolution, packed/paged MQA scoring, Top-K, block expansion, sparse attention, and hyperconnection norm/mix/combine. Wrappers own their model input contracts and internal Triton/native paths; unsupported NPU metadata is not silently redirected to a general reference. - Adapt rank-4 NPU KV pools through zero-copy views, so incompatible layouts fail rather than silently copying cache storage. - Keep NPU dispatch beside GPU entrypoints and preserve other platforms' behavior. Support sigmoid-gated normalization and retain the NPU hyperconnection compilation workaround for cached restarts. - Use graph-capturable PLE convolution for decode/target verify, preserving state updates, tracking, MTP, and ordinary prefill. Guard the newly merged CUDA verify-fusion path on NPU. - Maintain live graph metadata and draft-extend bounds; bypass CPU attention-input updates for Qwen QSA paths that consume device metadata. Avoid the CPU-fallback assertion in NPU QSA write planning. - Add and update regression tests for dispatch, indexing, cache layout, normalization, PLE, operator chains, and graph replay. Adapt tests to upstream runtime-context and graph-worker changes, including direct execution through registered CI entrypoints. ## Accuracy Tests ### GPQA Diamond The latest evaluation completed on October 12, 2026, after updating the companion kernel repository to `b01807d` (QSA Top-K and sparse attention dispatch adjustments). The kernel checkout was confirmed on the evaluation machine before testing. A post-run check of the same machine showed SGLang `7841e9bf1de41721c0ade41caad6738ac913909d` with a clean working tree; the exported results do not independently record the runtime source Git SHAs. | Implementation | SGLang revision | GPQA Diamond | | --- | --- | --- | | [Official model-card reference](https://huggingface.co/Qwen/Qwen3.8-Flash-Next/blob/main/README.md) | External reference | 91.7% | | Earlier Torch baseline | `64b0532544b9f784a5731b1c894d25347acc950b` | 181/198, 91.41% | | Early QSA Triton stage | `a02fa50abf08e3ba27d0051ac47b340b37a701a8` | 187/198, 94.44% | | September 17 integration | `e2f90ac5f4616cd7d521ef7bc19124dd86ed3b95` | 180/198, 90.91% | | September 22 integration | `e58dd411b006b55c62feb37f10c782a64f801ad5` | 181/198, 91.41% | | October 8 post-merge integration | `7841e9bf1de41721c0ade41caad6738ac913909d` | 181/198, 91.41% | | October 12 kernel-dispatch update | `7841e9bf1de41721c0ade41caad6738ac913909d` (post-run checkout check) | **183/198, 92.42%** | Evaluation settings: EvalScope 1.11.1, `temperature=0.9`, generation `seed=3407`, `n=1`, thinking enabled, `max_tokens=250000`, streaming, and client concurrency 32. Dataset seed is 42, with question and answer-choice shuffling enabled. The latest run took approximately 8 h 23 min and did not load a prior prediction cache. All 198 questions completed, with 183 correct and zero final request errors. One request timed out and was retried before completion. The earlier October 8 run used `max_tokens=260000` and counted one context-length rejection as incorrect; that rejection did not recur with the latest 250000-token output budget. The latest score is above the model-card reference in this individual run, but this is not a matched evaluation proving superiority or exact accuracy parity. The output-token limit also differs from the earlier runs, so the score change cannot be attributed solely to the kernel dispatch update. Historical revision attribution follows the previously documented run records; the early QSA Triton revision was reconstructed from a pre-run source snapshot. These results do not replace the separately recorded operator-level numerical limitations. ### Local regression and smoke checks - Focused post-merge SGLang regression: **451 passed, 7 skipped, 0 failed**; 23 CUDA-specific cases were excluded. This is not the full repository test suite. - After adding executable test entrypoints, the five affected files passed direct CI-style execution: **194 passed, 2 skipped, 0 failed**. These overlap the regression coverage above and are not an additional independent test count. - TP8 BF16 service startup, target-verify/draft-decode/draft-extend graph capture, short requests, and a batched long-prefill request passed with NEXTN/MTP. The long prompt exercised chunked prefill followed by decode. - PR-changed files in both repositories passed all applicable local pre-commit hooks. Final formatting and test-entrypoint changes do not alter the production computation. These checks do not establish all TP configurations, full-context coverage, multimodal accuracy, or long-run stability. Remote CI and reviewer approval remain separate merge requirements. ## Speed Tests and Profiling ### October 12 serving benchmark TP8 BF16 on NPU, with graph replay and NEXTN/MTP: 3 speculative steps, top-k 1, and 4 draft tokens. Server configuration uses a 4096-token prefill chunk, at most 8 running requests, static memory fraction 0.85, and disabled radix caching. Workload: `sglang-oai-chat`, 80 requests, concurrency 8, unlimited offered request rate, one warmup request, and request-body `temperature=0.01`. The `random` dataset mode uses ShareGPT text repeated/truncated to randomized input lengths; configured input/output lengths are 1024/1024 with range ratio 0.5 and benchmark seed 10130. This is not the original ShareGPT length distribution. EOS is ignored to reach the sampled output budgets. Thinking is not explicitly overridden in the benchmark request. +def layer_norm_ref(
+    x: torch.Tensor,
+    weight: torch.Tensor,
+    bias: torch.Tensor | None,
+    z: torch.Tensor | None = None,
+    eps: float = 1e-6,
+    group_size: int | None = None,
+    norm_before_gate: bool = True,
+    is_rms_norm: bool = False,
+) -> torch.Tensor:
+    """Reference implementation for both LayerNorm and RMSNorm (supports optional gate + group norm)."""
+    if is_rms_norm:
+        return rms_norm_ref(
+            x,
+            weight,
+            bias,
+            z=z,
+            eps=eps,
+            group_size=group_size,
+            norm_before_gate=norm_before_gate,
+            upcast=True,
+        )
+
+    dtype = x.dtype
+    x_f = x.float()
+    w_f = weight.float()
+    b_f = bias.float() if bias is not None else None
+    z_f = z.float() if z is not None else None
+
+    if z_f is not None and not norm_before_gate:
+        x_f = x_f * F.silu(z_f)
+
+    if group_size is None:
+        mean = x_f.mean(dim=-1, keepdim=True)
+        var = (x_f - mean).square().mean(dim=-1, keepdim=True)
+        rstd = torch.rsqrt(var + eps)
+        out = (x_f - mean) * rstd * w_f
+        if b_f is not None:
+            out = out + b_f
+    else:
+        hidden = x_f.shape[-1]
+        assert hidden % group_size == 0
+        ng = hidden // group_size
+        xg = x_f.view(*x_f.shape[:-1], ng, group_size)
+        mean = xg.mean(dim=-1, keepdim=True)
+        var = (xg - mean).square().mean(dim=-1, keepdim=True)
+        rstd = torch.rsqrt(var + eps)
+        xg = (xg - mean) * rstd
+        out = xg.reshape(*x_f.shape[:-1], hidden) * w_f
+        if b_f is not None:
+            out = out + b_f
+
+    if z_f is not None and norm_before_gate:
+        out = out * F.silu(z_f)
+
+    return out.to(dtype)
